question: What is the primary function of a stock card in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Listing the diagnostic results of admitted patients
options.B: Documenting the maintenance schedule of ward equipment
options.C: Tracking the exact quantity of a specific commodity available
options.D: Recording the daily attendance of nursing staff on duty

explanation: A stock card is specifically designed to monitor quantities of stored goods and supplies on hand. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h1)

question: Why is proper inventory control considered critical for clinical care?

options.A: It ensures essential supplies are available when patients need treatment
options.B: It eliminates the need for any central medical store warehouses
options.C: It completely prevents the expiration of drugs through automatic consumption
options.D: It replaces the need for keeping patient clinical case notes

explanation: Without proactive supply management, critical items run out, directly delaying patient care and interventions. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h1)

question: What does the running balance on a stock card represent?

options.A: The estimated budget allocated for purchasing new supplies
options.B: The total quantity of stock remaining after every transaction
options.C: The total number of items expired during the previous month
options.D: The maximum capacity that the storage shelf can hold

explanation: The balance field is updated continuously to reflect the exact physical count left on hand following receipts or issues. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h2)

question: Why must batch numbers and expiry dates be recorded on inventory control tools?

options.A: To calculate the total financial profit generated by the ward
options.B: To determine which pharmaceutical manufacturing company is cheapest
options.C: To track the individual names of nurses who dispensed the medication
options.D: To support the First-Expired, First-Out principle for patient safety

explanation: Tracking expiry dates ensures older stock is used before newer arrivals, preventing drug spoilage and wastage. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h2)

question: What does the reorder level indicate on a stock control system?

options.A: The absolute maximum quantity of items a storage shelf can hold
options.B: The minimum number of patients required to use a drug daily
options.C: The specific inventory threshold that triggers a new procurement request
options.D: The total amount of expired stock written off at year-end

explanation: Reaching the reorder level signals that stock is getting low enough to warrant placing a new order before reserves run out. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h3)

question: Why is maintaining a minimum stock level essential for a hospital ward?

options.A: It reduces the total financial cost of purchasing medical commodities
options.B: It guarantees that no medication will ever pass its printed expiry date
options.C: It eliminates the need to record daily issues on the stock card
options.D: It acts as a safety buffer to prevent stockouts during delivery delays

explanation: The minimum level provides a cushion of safety while waiting for requested supplies to be processed and delivered. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h3)

question: When is the best time to record a stock movement on a inventory card?

options.A: At the end of every financial quarter or fiscal year
options.B: Immediately as the items are received or issued out
options.C: Only when the stock balance reaches zero or causes a stockout
options.D: Whenever an external auditor visits the health facility

explanation: Prompt recording prevents forgotten transactions and maintains an accurate, real-time picture of inventory. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h4)

question: What is a frequent consequence of delaying entries on a stock card?

options.A: Lowering of the maximum stock ceiling level by the pharmacy
options.B: Automatic extension of the expiry dates on stored medications
options.C: Discrepancies between recorded balances and actual physical counts
options.D: Immediate delivery of emergency supplies from the central store

explanation: Waiting to record issues or receipts often leads to forgotten numbers and inventory mismatch. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h4)

question: Which inventory metric directly signals that a new purchase order must be placed?
explanation: The reorder level is specifically calculated to prompt procurement action before reserves hit zero. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h5)

question: What is the main risk of failing to base orders on actual consumption data?

options.A: Automatic conversion of physical stock cards into digital spreadsheets
options.B: Over-ordering unneeded items or running out of essential supplies
options.C: Immediate suspension of nursing licenses by the regulatory council
options.D: Prolonging the expiration dates of fragile pharmaceutical products

explanation: Using consumption data ensures orders match actual patient demand rather than random guesswork. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h5)

question: Why is physical inspection of delivered commodities mandatory before signing delivery notes?

options.A: To confirm quantities, check for damage, and verify acceptable expiry dates
options.B: To calculate the exact financial profit margins for the hospital management
options.C: To replace the need for entering the new items onto the stock card
options.D: To determine which delivery driver deserves an administrative commendation

explanation: Inspection protects the facility from accepting damaged, short-dated, or incomplete shipments. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: Which of the following actions should happen immediately after successfully inspecting incoming ward supplies?

options.A: Recording the new quantities and batch details on the stock card
options.B: Notifying the medical director that the facility budget is exhausted
options.C: Disposing of all the cardboard packing boxes into the general waste
options.D: Locking the items away in an unlabelled cupboard for safekeeping

explanation: Received stock must be logged immediately onto the inventory card to maintain an accurate running balance. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: What is a direct consequence of a sudden stockout of emergency medicines on a ward?

options.A: Immediate extension of the shelf-life of remaining medical products
options.B: Reduction in the total number of patients admitted to the hospital
options.C: Interrupted patient care and delayed emergency interventions
options.D: Automatic replenishment of supplies from central warehouses within minutes

explanation: When critical commodities run out, nurses cannot deliver timely, life-saving care. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h7)

question: Which practice is most effective for preventing the accumulation of expired stock in a medical store?

options.A: Stopping all routine physical stock audits and inventory counts
options.B: Hiding older products at the back of shelves to keep displays tidy
options.C: Enforcing the First-Expired, First-Out rule during daily dispensing
options.D: Ordering maximum quantities of every drug regardless of consumption rates

explanation: Using items with earlier expiry dates first ensures stock is consumed before it spoils. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h7)
